text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. text:
The history of forceful retching followed by immediate choking and chest pain is highly suggestive of a Mallory-Weiss tear or, less commonly, Boerhaave syndrome. I have requested a Chest X-Ray; while the patient mentioned "no significant finding," the clinical picture of vomiting, retching, and subsequent chest pain requires a more specific assessment. Can you describe the nature of the pain—specifically, does it worsen with coughing or take a breath, and is there any blood in the vomit?
